description: A tape loop that wears out: the play head reads it and the write head puts a slightly worse copy back in the same place, so the recording dulls, sags and drops out a little more on every pass

params.text: Sets how much is lost on each pass: at the bottom of its travel it takes hundreds of passes to hear a change, at the top the loop crumbles in minutes
Sets how much the play head wobbles in speed, and the wobble grows a little as the tape ages
Starts and stops recording onto the tape
Puts fresh tape in the machine: the loop goes back to the original recording with no wear, crossfaded over about 10ms so it does not click
Sets how soon the next play head starts: at the bottom of its travel the repeats run back to back, and at the top the next begins when the current one is halfway, so the loop plays over itself
Sets how much of what comes back at the return jack is written onto the tape, 0 to 1
Layers the input onto the tape while it keeps running, so a piece can be built up pass over pass
Sets how loud the overdub is written, and with it how much of the old tape the record head wipes: gentle sound-on-sound at the bottom of its travel, a punch-in replace at the top

inputs.text: The signal to record; the channel count of the cable at the moment recording starts sets how many tracks the tape has
A rising edge through 1V puts fresh tape in the machine
Added to the decay knob, a fifth of its travel per volt
Added to the wow knob, a fifth of its travel per volt
Added to the overlap knob, a fifth of its travel per volt
Added to the send knob, a fifth of its travel per volt
What comes back from whatever the send jack was patched into; it is written onto the tape as far as the send knob allows

outputs.text: The loop, ±5V, on as many channels as the tape was recorded with
0.1V for every completed pass of the tape, stopping at 10V: an odometer for how worn it is
A 1ms trigger at every heard loop restart, which with overlap up is twice per turn of the tape
A 0V to 10V ramp following the audible play head, one per heard repeat, clean of the wow so it stays a steady clock
The loop as read off the tape, for feeding an effect and bringing it back to the return jack; it carries the tape's own channel count

notes: nothing is heard until something has been recorded. Press rec or open the rec gate with a signal at the in jack, then let go.
the tape has one transport and several tracks: the wobble, the dropouts, the seam and the record crossfade are shared, so a stereo image stays locked together.
the age, eoc and ramp jacks are always single-channel, and the CV jacks, the two gates and the splice trigger read the first channel only.
menu: Monitor input — whether the signal at the input jack is heard at the output: While recording or empty, Always, or Never
Clear loop — empties the tape and starts again with nothing recorded
